tagline: iPhone vs Android, folding phones, and the gadgets everyone's carrying.
why: Your phone is the device you use most, so phones and gadgets are an easy topic with almost anyone. People compare iPhones and Androids, cameras and batteries, and talk about new launches like foldables and AI features. In Hong Kong you'll see the latest iPhones alongside Chinese brands like Huawei and Xiaomi, so knowing the landscape helps.

essentials.title: iOS vs Android
essentials.body: Apple's iPhone runs iOS; nearly everyone else runs Google's Android. iPhone users value the ecosystem; Android users value choice and customisation.

essentials.title: The launch calendar
essentials.body: Samsung launches Galaxy S phones in January-February and foldables in July. Apple launches iPhones every September. Chinese brands launch all year.

essentials.title: Cameras sell phones
essentials.body: Phone cameras compete on zoom, low light and video. Chinese brands often partner with camera makers like Leica and Hasselblad.

essentials.title: Foldables
essentials.body: Phones that fold like a book or a flip phone. Samsung, Huawei, Honor and others make them; Huawei even has a tri-fold.

essentials.title: Ecosystems
essentials.body: Watches, earbuds, tablets and laptops that work together: Apple's is the tightest, but Samsung, Xiaomi and Huawei are building their own.

essentials.title: AI features
essentials.body: Phones now pitch AI features like photo editing, summaries and assistants: Apple Intelligence, Galaxy AI, Gemini.

names.name: Apple
names.what: iPhone, AirPods, Apple Watch, Mac. The iPhone 17 line and the thin iPhone Air launched in 2025.

names.name: Samsung
names.what: The biggest Android maker; Galaxy S and Z Fold/Flip lines.

names.name: Huawei
names.what: Chinese giant that bounced back from US sanctions with its own chips and HarmonyOS; Mate and Pura lines.

names.name: Xiaomi
names.what: Value-focused Chinese brand, now also making EVs.

names.name: Google Pixel
names.what: Google's own phones, known for cameras and AI.

names.name: OPPO, vivo, OnePlus
names.what: Chinese brands known for cameras and fast charging.

names.name: Honor
names.what: Former Huawei sub-brand, strong in foldables.

names.name: Qualcomm
names.what: Maker of Snapdragon chips for Android phones.

names.name: Steve Jobs
names.what: Apple co-founder who launched the iPhone in 2007.

names.name: DJI
names.what: Chinese drone and camera maker; its Osmo Pocket and Action cameras are popular.

names.name: Garmin
names.what: Sports watch maker loved by runners and hikers.

timeline.event: First Android phone and the App Store.
First foldables; US sanctions hit Huawei.
Huawei Mate 60 Pro surprises with a Chinese-made advanced chip.
Apple Intelligence announced; Huawei's tri-fold phone.
iPhone Air; Apple's AI Siri delayed; Samsung's thinnest foldables.

now.headline: Thin is in
now.detail: Ultra-thin phones like the iPhone Air and Galaxy Edge, at the cost of battery life.

now.headline: AI features
now.detail: People debate whether phone AI is useful or a gimmick. Apple's Siri upgrade was delayed.

now.headline: Foldables mature
now.detail: Lighter, tougher foldables are becoming mainstream.

now.headline: Chinese brands rise
now.detail: Huawei leads China's market again; Xiaomi grows globally.

now.headline: Prices up
now.detail: Tariffs and memory chip costs push prices higher.

local.headline: Cheap iPhones
local.detail: Hong Kong has some of the world's lowest iPhone prices because there's no sales tax, so mainland visitors buy here.

local.headline: Two phones
local.detail: Many people carry two phones or dual SIMs for Hong Kong and mainland numbers.

local.headline: Sham Shui Po
local.detail: The district for electronics, accessories and repairs, including Golden Computer Arcade.

local.headline: Octopus on phone
local.detail: Paying with Octopus on iPhone or Android is standard.

debates.question: iPhone or Android?
debates.sides: Simplicity and ecosystem vs choice and value.

debates.question: Are foldables worth it?
debates.sides: Big screen in your pocket vs price and durability.

debates.question: Do you need to upgrade every year?
debates.sides: Phones last longer now; upgrades are smaller.
